Row
rō
n. (a line of things set in order; rendering Hebrew tur and ma'areket)
Old English rāw, a line. The breastplate's stones, the shewbread, and Solomon's cedar beams were all set in rows.

Biblical Definition

The breastplate of judgment held “four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle” (Exo 28:17), through the fourth row of “a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper” (Exo 28:20) — twelve stones for twelve tribes, carried on the high priest's heart. The shewbread was set “in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the LORD” (Lev 24:6). Solomon's inner court had “three rows of hewed stone, and a row of cedar beams” (1Ki 6:36). The bride's cheeks “are comely with rows of jewels” (Sng 1:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines row as a series of persons or things arranged in a continued line; a rank; a file.

expand to see more

ROW, n. A series of persons or things arranged in a continued line; a line; a rank; a file; as a row of trees; a row of houses.

Key Scripture

Exo 28:17 — "And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row."

Exo 28:20 — "And the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings."

Lev 24:6 — "And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the LORD."

1Ki 6:36 — "And he built the inner court with three rows of hewed stone, and a row of cedar beams."

Sng 1:10 — "Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold."

Modern Corruption

The rows of the breastplate are read for gemstone mysticism, and the text says whose names were on them and where they were carried.

expand to see more

Exodus 28 lists twelve stones in four rows, and the modern reader goes looking for what each stone means. The chapter tells him: “the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names” (v. 21), and Aaron “shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place” (v. 29). The rows are the tribes, and the point of the rows is that they were on the heart of the man who went in before God. Christ our High Priest carries His people the same way, by name, in rows, and no stone in the breastplate had a power of its own.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tur (H2905), a row, course; ma'areket (H4635), an arrangement, row; tor (H8447), a row, plait.

expand to see more

Hebrew tur (H2905) — a row, course of stones; Exodus 28:17–20, 39:10–13, 1 Kings 6:36, 7:2–4, Ezekiel 46:23.

Hebrew ma'areket (H4635) — a row, the shewbread's arrangement; Leviticus 24:6–7.

Hebrew tor (H8447) — a row, string of jewels; Song of Solomon 1:10–11.

Usage

"“Four rows of stones” — twelve names on one heart."

"“Two rows, six on a row” — the shewbread before the LORD."

"“Three rows of hewed stone, and a row of cedar beams” — Solomon's court."
